turns.prompt: G-001: the Viable System Model applied, and the first cost number in the package
turns.result:
The brief asked twice for Stafford Beer's VSM and was answered twice with the
body analogy. They are adjacent, not identical: the analogy says a house has
organs, the VSM says what has to be true for a system to survive an environment
trying to kill it. Applying it produced one finding the analogy could not.

THIS HOUSE HAD ALMOST NO S4. Every sensor in the package looked inward — leak,
freeze, CO, humidity. That is S3*, audit: it tells the house what is happening
to it, never what is about to. A house with audit and no intelligence can only
react, and arrives at every emergency with an empty battery, a half cistern and
a cold slab.

Driven by the reference pack, and specifically by the instruction at the foot

sheltered area, perimeter, wet-wall length, foundations, roof intersections,

model/schemes.mjs builds seven and computes exactly that list:

  S0 SPINE      the current design, as the opponent
  S1 ARMATURE   Rev. Walker's — two bays enclosed under a permanent five-bay roof
  S2 BRIDGE     20K Truss/Bridge — span the hill instead of cutting it
  S3 NARROW     Geraldine's + Sylvia 2/1, which was actually built on a steep
                site in Madison County NC — how narrow before it stops being generous
  S4 CORE       Myers' — one permanent core, everything else transient
  S5 PERCH      Sol Duc + Vermont Cabin — tiny footprint, vertical, lifted
  S6 TOWER      the 18x18 counter-hypothesis: do not assume the contour bar wins

Each names one transferable operation and one thing it must not copy, because

turns.prompt: Seven of eleven hero shots had the building falling out of the frame
turns.result:
S9-ASSEMBLY had never been rendered at all. When it finally was, the house sat
half off the bottom edge with a hillside filling the rest. tools/check/framing
was written to find out how many others were like that, by projecting each
scheme's bounding box through its own camera. Seven of eleven: the Tower losing
36% of itself, the Square 34%, the Perch 29%.

THE CAUSE, after three wrong fixes. makeShiftCamera builds an ARCHITECTURAL
camera — it looks at a point at its OWN height so the axis is horizontal and
verticals stay plumb, which means target.y is ignored and the lens shift is the
only vertical framing control. This code did not know that. It put the camera
high above the building and aimed it at the middle, expecting a tilt that
cannot happen, so the subject sat below a horizontal axis and fell off the
bottom.

I rewrote the DISTANCE formula three times before reading what the camera does.
Each rewrite moved the number and missed the cause: 7 failures, then 4, then 8.
The fit loop I then added "solved" it by retreating to 373 ft from an 18 ft
building — far enough that the depression angle flattened. In frame, and a
photograph of a hillside.

The camera height is what matters. Put it near the middle of the building and
the building is near the middle of the picture; distance then only decides how
much of the frame it fills, which is what the fit loop is actually for — it
expands until the corners fit, then bisects back to the tightest distance that
still works.

framed render now fails a check instead of shipping.
